newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on short covering.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher on short covering by dealers ahead of the long festive holidays, traders said.
The market is closed from February 6 to 11 for the twin festivals of Chinese New Year and Eid al-Fitr.
"There was some short covering from Europe and Australia but buying was very light," said one local trader.
Traders said a firmer Tokyo market also helped prices.
They said producers were unwilling to sell aggressively in anticipation of lower production in February due to less working days during the month and the onset of wintering.
At the close, benchmark March RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 302 cents ($1.21) a kg, up two cents from Tuesday.
March SMR 20 buyer was also up two cents to 297 ($1.19).
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 294 cents a kg, SMR CV at 357, SMR L at 338, SMR 5 at 303, SMR 10 at 295 and drum latex FOB at 235.
The INRO five-day moving average was 229.41 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Feb 4 against 229.26 on Feb 3. The daily indicator price was 230.68 versus 229.00.
